evidence.V1: Base-slab / column / capital-slab 'I' outline reads as a pillar in front, three-quarter and silhouette; symmetry error X/Y 0.0, centred on the 4x4 footprint.
evidence.V2: Big (shaft) and medium (square plinth + abacus, torus base, echinus) are clear, but small-scale detail is limited to one thin gold band under the capital.
evidence.V3: Proportions are sensible but built from plain primitives: a straight untapered cylinder between two square slabs, no entasis or exaggeration, so it reads partly stiff.
evidence.V4: Plinth and abacus carry consistent ~0.05-0.07 stud chamfers that catch a highlight line; torus base and echinus are smoothly rounded.
evidence.V5: Close-ups of base, shaft and capital are clean: no seams, pinches or z-fighting; only very faint smooth-shaded segment banding on the shaft.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in three values (dark slab, mid torus, light shaft) plus a single gold accent band; disciplined.
evidence.V7: 776 tris vs module target 800 (ceiling 2000): at target.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, chamfered made edges, stone hue + gold kit band; colourways (sandstone, brick) keep the same value structure.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Box, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, grid-corner origin; T1 tiling pass.

top_fixes: Add a slight taper/entasis or fluting to the shaft so it reads less like a stock cylinder
Add a small-scale detail tier (step moulding on the abacus edge or a second band at the base) to strengthen hierarchy
Give the capital a more shaped echinus so the transition from round shaft to square abacus is more confident
